cited_evidence.text: The multicomponent, non-dilute high/medium-entropy alloys (HEAs/MEAs) are a new class of structural metal alloys. HEAs/MEAs are under intense study due to intriguing combinations of properties such as high strength and high fracture toughness for certain alloys. The MEA fcc NiCoCr was shown to have the highest yield strength among the Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni family of equi-composition fcc alloys and a phenomenal fracture toughness at low temperature. The stable stacking fault energy (SFE) of NiCoCr was measured to be 22 ± 4 mJ m−2 whereas first-principles density-functional theory (DFT) studies on the random alloy showed a negative SFE at low temperatures, possibly becoming positive only around 300 K. Chemical short-range order (SRO) in NiCoCr has been suggested as the reason for the positive SFE, based on DFT. SRO was also deduced from EXAFS experiments but the interpretation relied on DFT. A new interatomic potential for the Ni–Co–Cr system fitted to extensive DFT suggested the SRO should be evident even at high annealing temperatures (e.g., 1650 K) and with a significant enhancement of the tensile yield strength as compared with the random alloy.
